observations.supported_pattern: Armor identity and exposure must be separately observable: rigid plate/mail/greaves and attachment logic remain first-read, while bounded upper-thigh openings supply deliberate exposure. Neutral eye-level task framing preserves the requested tone.
observations.candidate_pack_feedback: Prefer garment landmarks such as fitted plate bodice, high-waisted fauld, mail assembly, thigh gaps, buckles, and riveted joints over repeated anatomical coverage wording.

observations.supported_pattern: Rear-three-quarter full-figure framing, hair cleared above the opening, a visible nape fastening, and an opaque front-side wrap make open-back topology independently inspectable.
observations.candidate_pack_feedback: A candidate should bind opening perimeter, fastening, hair clearance, and visible front-side coverage as a coordinated composition recipe.

observations.supported_pattern: Generic paired side cutouts tend to reach the outer silhouette and read as open sides. A fully bounded window requires an explicit opaque outer-side band connecting the underarm-side seam to the high-hip seam.
observations.candidate_pack_feedback: Add 'closed sewn window with outer-side fabric bridge' as positive geometry and reject open-side silhouette, crop separates, and shadow gaps.

observations.supported_pattern: The slit is most testable when its endpoint is defined below a continuous closed hip yoke, with two finished vertical panel edges, the opposite skirt side, complete hem, and footwear all in frame.
observations.candidate_pack_feedback: Use garment-landmark relations such as closed hip yoke and finished panel endpoint; avoid redundant anatomical repetition while retaining the same topology.

observations.supported_pattern: Sheer semantics survive a complex scene when an opaque base, dry organza surface, visible seams and edges, transmitted background, and denser doubled folds coexist. Wetness and glazing stay spatially separate.
observations.candidate_pack_feedback: Keep material, boundary, transmission, and overlap-density evidence coupled. Garment-landmark wording and a neutral textile-editorial camera are sufficient; amber warmth should remain a separate optional lighting preference.

evidence_boundary: These are run-local findings from five final images and their preserved failure histories. They are not automatically promoted profiles, universal generation guarantees, audience-preference evidence, or user judgment.
